newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia kidnappers killed, rebel raids escalate.
newsitem.headline: Colombia kidnappers killed, rebel raids escalate.

text.p: Crack anti-kidnap police shot and killed five suspected guerrillas as they tried to abduct a civilian in southwest Colombia on Monday, police said.
National police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said the firefight broke out on the outskirts of Cali, Colombia's second-largest city, during a bungled attempt to kidnap a local landowner.

Serrano said he was investigating whether the men were leftist guerrillas, but did not confirm radio reports that all were members of the tiny Jaime Bateman rebel force -- a dissident faction of the now-defunct M-19 movement.
The incident coincided with the launch of an emergency defence plan in response to a recent wave of rebel raids on small towns across Colombia.

"The guerrilla wants to continue on its path of destruction and affecting the civilian population. It has a plan to attack towns and military convoys in a bid to kidnap troops," Serrano said after a weekly defence meeting.
Armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya said the new crisis plan, first outlined last week, would include recruiting 3,500 extra troops and creating new anti-guerrilla units.

The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army, and the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second-biggest rebel force, have staged dramatic raids on at least four towns since the start of the year.

The ELN attacked the town of Guaranda in northern Sucre province early on Monday. One rebel died in the fighting. The ELN staged a similiar assault on Sunday on the town of Vegachi in northwest Antioquia province on Sunday. Two police were killed in several hours of fighting.
